# @vllnt/convex-mcp — Full LLM Context

> Expose Convex functions as MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools via Streamable HTTP.
> This file contains everything needed to use the package correctly.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @vllnt/convex-mcp
```

Peer dependency: `convex` (>=1.0.0)

---

## Core Concepts

1. You define Convex functions (queries, mutations, actions) in your Convex project.
2. You create an MCP server config that maps those functions to named tools.
3. You mount the server on a route handler (Next.js App Router, Cloudflare Workers, etc.).
4. LLM clients connect via Streamable HTTP and call your Convex functions as MCP tools.

---

## Complete API Reference

### createMCPServer(config) -> ConvexMCPServer

Creates an MCP server. Auth is REQUIRED (default-deny — throws without it).

```typescript
import { createMCPServer } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";

const mcp = createMCPServer({
  // REQUIRED: auth configuration
  auth: {
    // REQUIRED: validate API key from Authorization: Bearer <key> header
    validate: (apiKey: string) => Promise<boolean> | boolean,

    // OPTIONAL: return a Convex auth token (JWT) to set on ConvexHttpClient
    // This populates ctx.auth in your Convex functions
    convexToken?: (apiKey: string) => Promise<string | undefined> | string | undefined,
  },

  // OPTIONAL: named MCP tools. Keys become tool names.
  tools?: Record<string, ToolDef>,

  // OPTIONAL: named MCP resources. Keys are URI template patterns.
  resources?: Record<string, ResourceDef>,

  // OPTIONAL: Convex deployment URL
  // Falls back to CONVEX_URL then NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL env var
  convexUrl?: string,

  // OPTIONAL: MCP server name (default: "convex-mcp")
  name?: string,

  // OPTIONAL: MCP server version (default: "0.1.0")
  version?: string,
});
```

Throws:
- If `auth.validate` is not provided.
- If no Convex URL is found.

### .handler(options?) -> { GET, POST }

Returns request handlers compatible with Next.js App Router route handlers.

```typescript
const { GET, POST } = mcp.handler();
// or
const { GET, POST } = mcp.handler({ allowedOrigins: ["https://example.com"] });
```

Both GET and POST accept a Request and return Promise<Response>.
POST validates Content-Type: application/json (returns 415 otherwise).

### query(ref, options?) -> ToolDef

Wraps a Convex query function reference as an MCP tool.

```typescript
import { query } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";

query(api.tasks.list, {
  args: v.object({ status: v.optional(v.string()) }),
  description: "List tasks by status",
})
```

### mutation(ref, options?) -> ToolDef

Wraps a Convex mutation. Same signature as query().

```typescript
import { mutation } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";

mutation(api.tasks.create, {
  args: v.object({ title: v.string() }),
  description: "Create a task",
})
```

### action(ref, options?) -> ToolDef

Wraps a Convex action. Same signature as query().

```typescript
import { action } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";

action(api.ai.summarize, {
  args: v.object({ documentId: v.id("documents") }),
  description: "Summarize a document",
})
```

### resource(ref, options?) -> ResourceDef

Wraps a Convex query as an MCP resource with a URI template.

```typescript
import { resource } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";

// Used as a key in the resources record:
resources: {
  "space://{id}": resource(api.spaces.get, {
    args: v.object({ id: v.id("spaces") }),
    description: "Get a space by ID",
  }),
}
```

### convexArgsToZod(argsValidator) -> z.ZodObject

Converts a Convex v.object() validator to a Zod object schema. Throws if not v.object().

### convertValidator(validator) -> z.ZodTypeAny

Converts any single Convex validator to a Zod schema. Recursive.
Throws UnsupportedValidatorError for unknown validator kinds.

### UnsupportedValidatorError

```typescript
import { UnsupportedValidatorError } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";
// Error: 'Unsupported Convex validator kind: "futureType". This may be from a newer version of Convex.'
```

---

## Types

```typescript
interface ServerConfig {
  auth: AuthConfig;
  tools?: Record<string, ToolDef>;
  resources?: Record<string, ResourceDef>;
  convexUrl?: string;
  name?: string;
  version?: string;
}

interface AuthConfig {
  validate: (apiKey: string) => Promise<boolean> | boolean;
  convexToken?: (apiKey: string) => Promise<string | undefined> | string | undefined;
}

interface ToolDef {
  ref: unknown;                    // Convex function reference (e.g. api.tasks.list)
  type: "query" | "mutation" | "action";
  args?: ConvexValidator;          // Convex v.object() validator
  description?: string;
}

interface ResourceDef {
  ref: unknown;                    // Convex function reference (must be a query)
  args?: ConvexValidator;
  description?: string;
}

interface HandlerOptions {
  allowedOrigins?: string[];
}

interface ConvexMCPServer {
  handler: (options?: HandlerOptions) => {
    GET: (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
    POST: (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
  };
}

type FunctionType = "query" | "mutation" | "action";
```

---

## Validator Mapping (Convex -> JSON Schema)

All Convex v.* types with their JSON Schema output:

| Convex | JSON Schema | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| v.string() | { "type": "string" } | |
| v.number() / v.float64() | { "type": "number" } | v.number() is alias for v.float64() |
| v.boolean() | { "type": "boolean" } | |
| v.null() | { "type": "null" } | |
| v.int64() | { "type": "string", "description": "64-bit integer as string..." } | JSON can't represent BigInt |
| v.bytes() | { "type": "string", "description": "Binary data as base64-encoded string" } | |
| v.id("table") | { "type": "string", "description": "Convex document ID for table 'table'" } | |
| v.literal("x") | { "const": "x" } | String, number, or boolean |
| v.array(v.X()) | { "type": "array", "items": X } | Recursive |
| v.object({...}) | { "type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...] } | Recursive |
| v.union(v.literal("a"), v.literal("b")) | { "enum": ["a", "b"] } | All-literal union -> enum |
| v.union(v.string(), v.number()) | { "anyOf": [...] } | Mixed union -> anyOf |
| v.optional(v.X()) | Removes field from "required" array | |
| v.record(k, v) | { "type": "object", "additionalProperties": V } | |
| v.any() | {} | Empty schema, accepts anything |

Unknown validator kinds throw UnsupportedValidatorError.

---

## Auth Flow

```
Request arrives with Authorization: Bearer <key>
  -> Extract API key from header
  -> Call auth.validate(apiKey)
     -> false: return 401 { "error": "Invalid API key." }
     -> true: continue
  -> If auth.convexToken defined: call auth.convexToken(apiKey)
     -> If returns token: ConvexHttpClient.setAuth(token)
  -> Process MCP request
```

Missing Authorization header -> 401 { "error": "Missing API key. Provide an Authorization header." }

---

## Error Handling

All Convex function errors are caught and replaced with a generic message:

Tool call errors:
```json
{ "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Function execution failed" }], "isError": true }
```

Resource read errors:
```json
{ "text": "{\"error\":\"Resource read failed\"}", "mimeType": "application/json" }
```

Original error messages are NEVER forwarded to the MCP client (may contain PII).

To surface specific errors, return them as part of your function's success response:
```typescript
// In your Convex function:
if (invalid) return { success: false, error: "Title required" };
return { success: true, id };
```

---

## Complete Example

```typescript
// convex/mcp.ts
import { createMCPServer, query, mutation, action, resource } from "@vllnt/convex-mcp";
import { api } from "./_generated/api";
import { v } from "convex/values";

export const mcp = createMCPServer({
  auth: {
    validate: async (key) => key === process.env.MCP_API_KEY,
    convexToken: async (apiKey) => {
      // Optional: exchange API key for Convex JWT
      return undefined;
    },
  },
  tools: {
    // Query tool (read-only, cached)
    list_tasks: query(api.tasks.list, {
      args: v.object({
        status: v.optional(v.union(
          v.literal("todo"),
          v.literal("in_progress"),
          v.literal("done"),
        )),
      }),
      description: "List tasks, optionally filtered by status",
    }),

    // Mutation tool (write, transactional)
    create_task: mutation(api.tasks.create, {
      args: v.object({
        title: v.string(),
        description: v.optional(v.string()),
        tags: v.optional(v.array(v.string())),
      }),
      description: "Create a new task",
    }),

    // Action tool (side effects, external APIs)
    summarize: action(api.ai.summarize, {
      args: v.object({
        documentId: v.id("documents"),
      }),
      description: "Generate an AI summary of a document",
    }),
  },
  resources: {
    "task://{id}": resource(api.tasks.get, {
      args: v.object({ id: v.id("tasks") }),
      description: "Get a task by ID",
    }),
  },
});
```

```typescript
// app/api/mcp/route.ts
import { mcp } from "@/convex/mcp";
export const { GET, POST } = mcp.handler();
```

Environment variables:
```
CONVEX_URL=https://your-deployment.convex.cloud
MCP_API_KEY=your-secret-key
```

---

## Deployment Notes

- Works with any platform supporting Web Fetch API (Request -> Response)
- Next.js App Router: export { GET, POST } from handler()
- Vercel Hobby: 10s timeout (fine for queries/mutations)
- Vercel Pro: 60s timeout
- Vercel Pro + Fluid Compute: 800s timeout (for long-running actions)
- Set maxDuration in route file: `export const maxDuration = 60;`

---

## Security Summary

- Default-deny: auth.validate is REQUIRED, server throws without it
- Generic errors: Convex errors never leak to MCP client
- No function-level authz in v1: valid API key = access to all exposed tools
- Service account model: by default ctx.auth is null; use convexToken hook for identity
- Scope tools carefully: only expose functions the key holder should access

---

## Known Limitations

1. Validator duplication: must provide v.object() validators alongside function refs (FunctionReference has no runtime schema)
2. No per-tool authorization: a valid key accesses all tools (create separate servers for different access levels)
3. Service account model: no per-user identity by default (use convexToken for identity propagation)
4. No built-in rate limiting: use platform-level rate limiting
